{{Otheruses|Yuga Daigongen (disambiguation)}}
'''Yuga Daigongen''' (瑜伽大権現) is a syncretic deity of {{ill|Mountain worship|en|Mountain worship|qid=Q93697439|lt=mountain worship}} and {{ill|Shugendō|en|Shugendō|qid=Q1483875|lt=Shugendō}} originating from {{ill|Bizen Province|en|Bizen Province|qid=Q1053688|lt=Bizen Province}}'s {{ill|Yuga Mountain|ja|由加山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuga Mountain|qq=}}. The deity's {{ill|Honji suijaku|en|Honji suijaku|qid=Q3080781|lt=Honji Buddha}} are {{ill|Amitābha|en|Amitābha|qid=Q236242|lt=Amida Nyorai}} and {{ill|Bhaisajyaguru|en|Bhaisajyaguru|qid=Q854773|lt=Yakushi Nyorai Medicine Buddha}}. During the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}} order in the early Meiji period, the deity was renamed "Sōō Daibosatsu" (相応大菩薩) to comply with the new regulations but has since reverted to its original name and is enshrined at {{ill|Yugasan Rendaiji|ja|瑜伽山蓮台寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yugasan Rendaiji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.

== Origin ==
According to legend, {{ill|Gyōki|en|Gyōki|qid=Q1136664|lt=Gyōki}} received a revelation in a dream saying, "This mountain is a peerless sacred land. Establish a temple here, practice the three mysteries of {{ill|yoga in Buddhism|ja|瑜伽|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yoga|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24886203}}, and worship me as Yuga Daigongen." Following this revelation, Gyōki founded the temple on the mountain in the fifth year of {{ill|Tenpyō|en|Tenpyō|qid=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyō}} (733 CE). He enshrined Amida Nyorai and Yakushi Nyorai, marking the beginning of the Yuga Daigongen faith.<ref>Rendaiji Engi (Temple Record).</ref> 

The faith further developed when Yuga Mountain was referred to as "New Kumano Nachisan," aligning with the {{ill|Five Schools of Shugendō|ja|五流修験道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Schools of Shugendō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. According to the records of the Five Streams’ Honzan-based {{ill|Goryū Sontakuin|ja|五流尊瀧院|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goryū Sontakuin|qq=}}, the mountain's temples—Rendaiji (Nachisan), Goryū Sontakuin (Hongū), and Shokōji (Shingū)—were collectively known as the "New Kumano Gongen Three Shrines."

== Overview ==
Yuga Daigongen is known as the "Deity of Disaster Prevention." The deity was deeply revered by successive lords of the {{ill|Okayama Domain|en|Okayama Domain|qid=Q903497|lt=Okayama Domain}}, starting with {{ill|Ikeda Tsugumasa|en|Ikeda_Tsugumasa|qid=Q28131624|lt=Ikeda Tsugumasa}}. It also became one of the most significant pilgrimage destinations in the {{ill|Seto Inland Sea|en|Seto Inland Sea|qid=Q231312|lt=Seto Inland Sea}} region. Alongside {{ill|Konpira Gongen|lt=Konpira Gongen|lt=Konpira Daigongen|ja|金毘羅大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konpira Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 金毘羅権現}}, it was worshiped as one half of the "Dual Pilgrimage," with devotees visiting both shrines once in their lifetime to pray for the fulfillment of their wishes.<ref name="yugasan">[http://www.yugasan.jp/engi.html Yugasan Rendaiji – Historical Record]</ref>

== Shinbutsu Bunri and Haibutsu Kishaku ==
The {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}} order of 1868, followed by the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|en|Haibutsu kishaku|qid=Q702298|lt=Haibutsu kishaku}} movement, led to the abolition of Yuga Daigongen as a Shugendō deity. Although {{ill|Yugasan Rendaiji|ja|瑜伽山蓮台寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yugasan Rendaiji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} narrowly avoided closure in 1873, it was forcibly separated into the {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|en|Shingon Buddhism|qid=Q550182|lt=Shingon Buddhism}}-affiliated Rendaiji and the {{ill|Yuga Shrine|ja|由加神社本宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuga Shrine|qq=}}.
